questions.stem: Which type of radiation is used as a medical tracer and why?

options.text: Alpha, because it is strongly ionising
Beta, because it has a long half-life
Gamma, because it can pass through the body and be detected externally
Alpha, because it can pass through the body easily

questions.explanation: Gamma radiation is used for medical tracers because it is highly penetrating and can pass through the body to be detected by external cameras. It is also weakly ionising, which means it causes less damage to body tissue. The tracer isotope should also have a short half-life so it decays quickly after the procedure.

questions.stem: In industrial thickness gauging of metal sheets, which type of radiation would be most suitable?

options.text: Any type would work equally well

questions.explanation: Gamma radiation is used for gauging thick metal sheets because it is the most penetrating and can pass through metal. Beta radiation would be suitable for thin materials like paper or aluminium foil, while alpha would be stopped too easily. The choice depends on the thickness and density of the material being measured.
